name: search-relevance
description: SYNTHETIC passage-level relevance set for the Search endpoint (POST /api/v1/search/), not the chat engine. Every document in the corpus was written for this repository, so a score here says the ranking behaves as designed - it is NOT a measurement of accuracy on any institution's documents. Sixteen documents: the nine institutional ones the chat benchmarks use, plus seven distractors that reproduce the failure modes observed on a real, OCR-heavy corpus - a staff rulebook that repeats 'attendance', 'minimum', 'late' and 'examination' about a different population; long lecture notes whose many chunks share common words ('time required', 'minimum', 'library', 'fine'); a transport circular with a colliding identifier and Saturday/late vocabulary; and four short OCR-damaged fragments of the kind dense retrievers rank close to almost any query. A passage is relevant when it belongs to the named document AND contains the evidence text (case- and whitespace-insensitive), so the labels survive a change of chunk size. Relevance is topical, as a reader of search results would judge it, not 'answers the question'. Cases carry a fixed split: thresholds may be chosen on 'dev' only, and 'test' is reported. Governed and immutable at this version, like the chat benchmarks: a change is s2.
